title: Decision Trees in Machine Learning (CART)
description: Breiman's CART grows decision trees by recursive splitting on the feature that best separates the data — interpretable models you can read as rules. The explorer uses them where transparency matters.

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(1001)
# Expected-value fold-back: launch decision with two market scenarios.
# Branch A: launch now. Branch B: pilot first ($10k), then decide.
p_good=0.6
pay_launch_good=200000; pay_launch_bad=-80000
pay_pilot= -10000
# pilot reveals market perfectly for simplicity
ev_launch=p_good*pay_launch_good+(1-p_good)*pay_launch_bad
ev_pilot=pay_pilot + p_good*pay_launch_good + (1-p_good)*0  # abandon if bad
print(f"EV(launch now)=${ev_launch:,.0f}")
print(f"EV(pilot first)=${ev_pilot:,.0f}")
print(f"recommendation={'PILOT FIRST' if ev_pilot>ev_launch else 'LAUNCH NOW'}")
print(f"value_of_information=${ev_pilot-ev_launch:,.0f}")
print("DEMO_OK")
demo.output:
EV(launch now)=$88,000
EV(pilot first)=$110,000
recommendation=PILOT FIRST
value_of_information=$22,000
DEMO_OK
demo.note: Runnable demo program verified by execution during the database build.

architecture: Splits are chosen by impurity reduction (Gini/entropy); growth stops on validation criteria; pruning removes overfit branches. Each leaf's rule reads as plain logic.
implementation_status: Public method, established (Breiman et al. 1984). Prototype validated in this build (executed 2026-10-21).
provenance: Breiman, L. et al. (1984). Classification and Regression Trees. Wadsworth. Public record.
